key_findings: Heavenly Court vs Vulture Peak: the Court is stock-maintaining; Vulture Peak is incremental-expansion, winning on efficiency and innovation
Wukong's six career stages: from Stone Monkey King (L0) to Victorious Fighting Buddha (L9) to Retirement (L10); satisfaction follows a U-shape
100% of the five demon groups were acquired; none had an independent IPO, revealing the dependent demon economy
Bimawen is the lowest Heavenly Court post (unranked); Great Sage Equal to Heaven is an empty title without emolument
The pilgrimage is essentially an 'equity incentive': future options (Buddhahood) in exchange for present low-wage labor
cross_concept_insight: The Journey to the West business model reveals an 'inside/outside the system' duality: Heaven is a rigid state enterprise; Vulture Peak an efficient private enterprise; demons are startups; Wukong is a founder-to-partner transition case
business_lessons: Organizational efficiency: flat + delegated > pyramidal + centralized (Vulture Peak vs Heavenly Court)
Career curve: going it alone fails; teamwork succeeds (Wukong's career transition)
Startup trap: dependent businesses cannot IPO independently (demon groups)
Incentive mechanism: equity/options > fixed salary (pilgrimage project design)
Compliance risk: illegal business models inevitably draw regulatory crackdowns (demons eating people)
